Below is a Boolean formula in conjunctive normal form. Each numbered line is a clause; a clause is satisfied when at least one of its literals is true, and "not x" is the negation of variable x.

Clauses:
1. (not tree or book)
2. (ring or not sea)
3. (not horn or hill or map)
4. (iron or not fork)
5. (sea or not iron)
6. (not sea or harp)
7. (not wall or key)
8. (hill or not horn or not salt)

22. (bell or not ring)
23. (bread or fork)

25. (not salt or bear or horn)

36. (king or ring)

Choose any assignment that satisfies all the clauses. What value does fork take in your assignment? Answer with one word: True or False.

Clauses:
1. (not sea or ring)

5. (iron or nut)
6. (iron or not fork)
7. (snow or tree)

16. (not salt or bear or horn)
17. (cave or wall)
18. (sea or not ring)
19. (book or plum)
20. (not wall or key)
21. (lock or not iron)
22. (bell or not ring)
23. (fork or bread)
24. (harp or not sea)

Choose any assignment that satisfies all the clauses. What value does fork take in your assignment? Answer with one word: True or False.
